newsitem.title: BRAZIL: HSBC to take over Brazil's Bamerindus.
newsitem.headline: HSBC to take over Brazil's Bamerindus.

text.p: The Hong Kong & Shanghai Banking Corp was given approval Wednesday by Brazil's Central Bank to take over troubled private banking group Bamerindus, Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola said.

Loyola told reporters he gave permission to Central Bank officials to sign an agreement with HSBC to assume Bamerindus' assets and liabilities and turn it into a new bank with an immediate $1.0 billion capital injection.
Loyola said the HSBC offer was the best of two proposals to salvage Bamerindus, the other coming from Swiss bank Union de Banques Suisses (UBS) in association with local bank Banco Graphus.
"The Central Bank opted for the alternative, which in our view would better address public interest, that being the proposal from the (HSBC)," Loyola said.
He added that the operation involved the "formation of a new bank for the purchase of assets and liabilities" of Bamerindus and the use of special PROER credit lines to make the operation possible.

Loyola did not specify the amount of PROER funds that would be used, but said they would be used principally to allow federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal to assume Bamerindus' mortgage portfolio.
"In addition, there will be an immediate capitalization of the new bank through the input by (HSBC) of funds of the value of $1.0 billion," Loyola said.
He added the new bank would assume all Bamerindus international obligations and credit.
